title: ISL 2026-27 to Proceed With 13 Teams as AIFF Mulls One-Season Relegation Freeze
excerpt: Diamond Harbour FC's failure to pay participation fees leaves Indian football's top flight with a reduced roster, prompting the federation to consider suspending relegation for the upcoming season.
body:
• The Indian Super League will proceed with 13 clubs after Diamond Harbour FC failed to pay the ₹55 lakh second instalment of its participation fee by the extended August deadline.
  • The AIFF is considering a one-season suspension of relegation, subject to approval from the league governing council and executive committee.
  • The season has been delayed from its original September 4 start date and will now begin only after the FIFA international window closes on October 6.
  • Churchill Brothers have entered the ISL after acquiring Jamshedpur FC's licence for a symbolic ₹100, following Tata Steel's exit from the club.

Indian football's top-flight league will kick off its 13th season with one fewer team than planned, after a turbulent off-season that saw a club withdrawal, a licence transfer and the barring of newly promoted champions from participation.

Diamond Harbour's Dramatic Fall

Diamond Harbour FC, the Indian Football League champions who earned promotion by winning their third consecutive title across three tiers of Indian football, were barred from the ISL after failing to complete payment of the ₹1.1 crore participation fee. The West Bengal-based club paid the first instalment of ₹55 lakh but missed the extended deadline for the second payment.

The club's rapid rise — from I-League 3 to I-League 2 to IFL champions in successive seasons — had been one of Indian football's most compelling stories. But a West Bengal government investigation into the club's source of funds cast a shadow over its participation, and the fee default sealed its exclusion.

Jamshedpur Out, Churchill Brothers In

The league's contraction was compounded by Jamshedpur FC's withdrawal. Tata Steel, which had backed the club since its ISL inception, pulled out on July 31, hours after the first fee instalment deadline. The club's entire stake was transferred to Goa's Churchill Brothers for a symbolic ₹100, marking the first ownership transfer of its kind in ISL history.

Churchill Brothers subsequently paid the full ₹1.1 crore fee on August 14, securing their place in the top flight.

Relegation Freeze Under Consideration

With only 13 teams remaining — down from 14 last season — the AIFF is now weighing a one-season suspension of relegation. The proposal, first reported on August 22, requires approval from the league's governing council and executive committee.

Mohammedan Sporting Club, who finished bottom of the table last season and were relegated, had lobbied the AIFF for reinstatement as a replacement for Diamond Harbour. General Secretary Wasim Akram formally wrote to the federation requesting consideration, but the appeal has not resulted in their inclusion.

Season Format and Media Rights

The 2026-27 season will return to the double round-robin, home-and-away format — a significant upgrade from last season's truncated single-leg round-robin, which was forced by the expiry of the Master Rights Agreement between the AIFF and its former commercial partner FSDL.

On the commercial front, ISL clubs have opened direct negotiations with Zee and Sony Sports over a four-season media rights deal after the tender attracted only a single bid. Google has also held discussions about potentially making matches available live on YouTube.

"The ISL is likely to start only in October after the FIFA window. We are going with 13 teams in the ISL."

— Senior AIFF official, via PTI

For diaspora fans who followed last season's compressed schedule with frustration, the return of a full home-and-away format is a welcome development. But the structural instability — club exits, fee defaults and an uncertain broadcast arrangement — underscores the challenges facing Indian club football as it tries to build a sustainable commercial model.
